title: Threshold registry — threshold-contract SoT shape (TRK-339 WS1a / #1200 D2)
description: Shape contract for rule-packs/threshold-registry.yaml, the standalone threshold-contract SoT decided by epic #1200 D2 (standalone YAML registry: language-neutral, schema-validatable). STRICT at every level (additionalProperties:false) — this file is the hand-authored contract (since D-A PR-3), so a typo'd field or a mis-typed value must fail at author/CI time, not surface later as a silently-dropped threshold identity. Enforcement note: it covers all packs/keys, but the enforcement path this registry first serves is the 18-key repair line (#1196 / TRK-337). Validated BEFORE any generation stage by scripts/tools/lint/check_threshold_registry.py (pre-commit + CI).
$comment: Cross-entry constraints that JSON Schema cannot express — every keys.<k>.pack must exist under packs, every critical_of must name a key in the same pack, every deprecated_aliases target must name an existing key while its OLD spelling must NOT be an active key, every retired_keys entry must be no active key, on neither side of an alias, and replaced by an active key or null — are enforced by check_threshold_registry.py: the document (hand-authored since D-A PR-3) must be a fixed point of projecting it to scaffold's RULE_PACKS shape and extracting it again (fixed_point_problems in _registry_lib.py), which applies every fail-loud rule of build_registry_doc to the authored file. metric_class is an enum on purpose: adding a new class is a deliberate contract change and must touch this schema.

version.$comment: Registry FORMAT version (not the platform release). Bump only with a migration note in the file header.

deprecated_aliases.title: Retired threshold-key spellings still honored during their transition window (#1231)

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.$comment: old spelling -> canonical key. The old spelling stays pattern-legal (it WAS a key); the target must be an existing active key and the old spelling must not be — cross-checked fail-loud by the fixed-point check, not expressible here. This section is the alias SSOT: its one runtime mirror, Go's pkg/config/aliases.go deprecatedKeyAliases, is pinned to it by pkg/config/aliases_registry_test.go.

deprecated_aliases.$comment: Optional and sparse: present only while at least one alias window is open. Authored here (since D-A PR-3; _registry_lib.DEPRECATED_KEY_ALIASES reads this section).

retired_keys.title: Threshold keys retired from the contract: no rule pack reads them any more (#3829)

replaced_by.description: The active key that replaces it; null when nothing does.

hint.description: One English sentence for the operator, printed after the generated text that names replaced_by.

retired_keys.$comment: The shared key verdict judges a key in this section unread / error / reason retired in every layer, whatever reads it; tenant-api's batch unset admits it. Cross-entry rules (not an active key, on neither side of deprecated_aliases, replaced_by an active key or null, tracking set) are enforced by the fixed-point check (_registry_lib.retired_key_problems). Its `<key>_critical` is retired with it (replaced by `<replaced_by>_critical`, the shape an alias maps), so that tier must not be an active key either. Generated into Go as pkg/config/retired_threshold_keys_gen.go by check_threshold_registry.py --regen. When an alias window closes, the old spelling moves here.

packs.title: Pack-level metadata (one entry per rule pack, kubernetes included)

keys.title: Flat threshold-key identity map (the contract body)

pack.$comment: Must name an entry under packs (cross-checked by the gate, not expressible here).

tier.$comment: defaults = emitted by the platform-defaults path (reachable per TRK-337); optional_overrides = declared without a value — the platform recognises the key and asserts no number for it. WIRED as of #1310: the flat keys of this tier are shipped on the runtime `optional_overrides:` list (helm values + both onboarding `_defaults.yaml` producers), so a tenant sets one and resolveDeclaredRows emits it; `<base>_critical` keys stay off that list and resolve via resolveCriticalRows off defaults[base] instead. What the tier does NOT mean is 'not yet done' — an unset declared key is silent by design. Nor is the tier one population: of its 25 keys, the 9 flat ones are exactly the A-class of the 18 dead keys, while the other 16 are `<base>_critical` — and 5 of those are settable by a tenant TODAY because their base is a shipped chart default, so 'off the declared list' must never be read as 'dormant'. Which bucket a key lands in decides what a tenant can actually do with it, which is why tier is a load-bearing field, not decoration.

metric_class.description: Semantic class of the threshold key (REQUIRED on every key — #1200 WS1a PR-2). saturation = bounded-resource usage/backlog with a paired symptom metric (CURATED, product-facing: drives scaffold's educational _critical annotation + portal metricClass hints — membership changes are deliberate product decisions, not mechanical edits). capacity = fill level of a bounded space/allocation (disk, tablespace, log, parts, memory budget) without the paired-symptom curation. throughput = work-rate volume (qps, ops/s, req/s, msg/s). latency = time-to-complete or stall accumulation (GC pause, wait-time rate). replication = replica sync health (lag, under-replication, replication queue). state = discrete expected-value/topology invariant (cluster color, broker count, active controllers, consumers present). efficiency = cache/buffer effectiveness & waste (hit/miss ratio, evictions). errors = undesirable-event rate (deadlocks).
metric_class.$comment: Authored on every key, _critical derivatives included (since D-A PR-3 there is no inheritance step: the file states each class). Adding a new class is a contract change: extend this enum deliberately and define it in the description.

arming.description: Whether the Helm chart ships this key's value (D-A A1, #3773). default = shipped enabled: thresholdConfig.defaults and the dev conf.d template are GENERATED from this set; only on tier:defaults. operator = not shipped; the deployment must supply it. (Not `off`: YAML 1.1 reads an unquoted off as false.)
arming.$comment: REQUIRED on every key that is not a <base>_critical, FORBIDDEN on a <base>_critical (it follows its base). That split depends on the derived critical_of, so _registry_lib.arming_problems enforces it through the fixed-point check, as it does the rule that a default key is portable and unblocked unless it records default_exception.

portability.description: Whether ONE value of this key carries across deployments. portable = yes. ratio_pending = an absolute value that does not; the fix is a ratio form (#1320). site_specific = no universal value exists. Required on shipped keys too, so a shipped absolute value is caught.
portability.$comment: Same presence rule as arming. A portable, unshipped, unblocked key in the defaults tier is a validation candidate (the D-A A2 input), derived by _registry_lib.validation_candidates — never authored.

portability_reason.$comment: Why one value does not carry, one line in English. Required iff portability is not portable (the allOf below); _registry_lib.arming_problems also rejects surrounding whitespace, since the generated surfaces splice it into # comments.

portability_reason_zh.$comment: The same reason in Traditional Chinese; the generated helm values and rule-pack headers render this one.

blocker.description: Something other than validation that stops the key from shipping, with the issue tracking it. A default key cannot carry one.

default_exception.description: Records why a non-portable value ships anyway (arming: default with portability other than portable), with the issue that resolves it. Forbidden anywhere else (enforced by _registry_lib.arming_problems).

validation.description: What a shipped value rests on (D-A A2). REQUIRED on every arming: default key; an operator key may carry it ahead of its promotion. vendor = one source that uses this very value. consensus = two or more sources from different organisations whose values bracket it (ends included).
validation.$comment: No relation (equal / stricter / looser) is authored: it is the source's value against the registry's, checked by _registry_lib.validation_problems, so it cannot go stale when the value changes. The cross-field rules (vendor: one source, equal value; consensus: >= 2, distinct org and url, value within their range; required iff arming is default; forbidden beside value_counterexample on a default key) live in the gate, not here. Whether two organisations are independent is a reviewer's call. The promtool test that binds the key is tests/rulepacks/armed-<key>_test.yaml, held by tests/rulepacks/test_armed_key_binding.py.

quote.$comment: Copied from the page at url: the expression or sentence that states the number.

value.$comment: The source's threshold, in this key's unit.

tier.$comment: The severity the source alerts at, when it states one. Informational: the registry value here is the warning tier.

critical_of.$comment: DERIVED, never authored: present iff the key ends in _critical and its base key exists in the same pack. Names the base key.

dimensions.$comment: AUTHORED (#3475, ADR-038 §11): the labels this key's rule pack reads per value — its threshold normalisation keeps them through `max by(...)`. Rendered into the runtime `dimensions:` declaration (helm values, dev template, try-local seed); the exporter serves a dimensional key only when every label of its selector is declared there. tests/shared/test_dimension_registry.py pins it both ways to the packs.

value_counterexample.$comment: Sparse. Records that the ADR-030 reference-validation library produced a measured case THIS value gets wrong, so every face that hands the number over can hand over what we know about it (#1176 / #1320 D1: the platform does not pick numbers for tenants). ⛔ It is NOT a verdict that the value is wrong: that library is a sampling probe and its README's anti-Goodhart clause forbids treating it as a spec — re-tuning a threshold to satisfy a waveform invalidates the measurement. Stating the observation and letting the reader judge is the whole point. Absence means 'no counter-example measured', never 'value validated'.

issue.$comment: GitHub issue carrying the measurement, so the claim is auditable rather than folklore.

direction.$comment: over_fire = a BENIGN scenario crossed this threshold (false alarm). under_fire = a REAL fault stayed under it (missed detection). The two are not interchangeable — a blanket 'these values are too low' caveat is false for the under_fire ones, which is exactly why this is an enum and not prose.

observed.$comment: The measured scenario in ONE clause, phrased as an observation ('a routine backup batch reaches 560 processes'), not as an instruction. ⛔ Single line: every consumer splices this into a `#` comment, and a newline puts the tail at column 0 — the written `_defaults.yaml` stops being valid YAML and the tenant's config fails to load. ⚠️ This `pattern` catches an EMBEDDED newline only. It does NOT catch a TRAILING one — jsonschema matches with `re.search` and Python's `$` also matches just before a final newline, so `observed: |` (the natural YAML spelling for a long clause) passes here. The enforcer for the trailing/blank/padded cases is `_registry_lib.require_counterexample`, which every composer calls; this pattern is the portable half. Do not read a green schema run as 'single line, enforced' (#1344).

observed_zh.$comment: The same observation in Traditional Chinese. ⛔ Present for every counter-example the platform ships — enforced by `tests/lint/test_counterexample_coverage.py`, not optional-in-practice — because the ZH surfaces include `<tenant>.yaml`, the one file a tenant opens, and a Chinese frame wrapped around an English clause is a worse read than either language alone (owner decision, #1344; CodeRabbit had asked for the reverse and was refused on the grounds that `desc` is 67/67 English — that argument holds for `desc`, which no tenant-facing sentence embeds). ⚠️ It is SCHEMA-optional so that the field can be added to a new key in a follow-up commit without breaking the registry; the composers fall back to `observed` rather than rendering nothing, because silence must keep meaning 'not measured'. The gate is what makes the fallback unreachable in shipped data.
